heading: Purpose
text:
### Purpose [LNLS.1.1]

`linear_scan: false` is a capability setting that restricts DS
programs to a subset where every runtime data-structure operation is
provably sub-linear in the working-memory population or series depth.
The name reflects the implementation guarantee, not the programming
model: the compiler enforces language-level constraints whose
collective effect is that no engine subsystem scans a list or array
proportional to fact count.

A program compiled with `linear_scan: false` trades away certain language
features — dynamic strings, JSON slots, unbounded sketch aggregations,
and range-only join conditions — in return for algorithmic guarantees
that hold at any WM population size.
